headline: Highest risk is medium cascading error: Great Expectations can consume Argo Workflows outputs as validation inputs, but the pair lacks direct evidence of default shared channels or unsafe automation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and Great Expectations reads files/data sources, so a manual or shared-workspace bridge could carry malicious instructions into content that B parses. However, neither profile shows a default shared channel, and Argo has allowlisted egress while Great Expectations has no network egress, so the pathway is not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies Argo-produced text into a Great Expectations config or documentation file
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the two agents into distinct directories
Require human review before Great Expectations consumes Argo-generated files
Add provenance labels to shared artifacts
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text as instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or schema validation at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. The profiles do not show secrets handling, shared OAuth, or default upload of file contents, so leakage is possible mainly through an unusual shared workspace or manual transfer, with limited evidence of sensitive classes beyond operational artifacts.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains sensitive artifacts and validation outputs
IF either agent is configured to ingest those files into reports or docs
mitigations: Store each agent's files in separate folders
Remove sensitive fields from artifacts before handoff
Restrict workspace permissions to least privilege
Review generated validation outputs before sharing
requires-engineering: implement redaction at export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows has REST/GRPC API access and allowlisted egress; Great Expectations can install packages and write files. The profiles do not show overlapping unrestricted writes to the same directory or shared mutable resources, so direct conflict is not default. A conflict appears only if an operator points both at the same workspace or mutable pipeline state.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF both modify the same pipeline or dependency state without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Pin package versions before validation runs
Avoid concurrent edits to shared configs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce artifacts and Great Expectations can consume validation inputs, so B may treat A's outputs as authoritative unless an explicit verification step exists. The profiles do not document such a check, and the interaction is plausible in default data-engineering workflows, though not proven to be fully automated.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Argo-produced artifacts as test inputs
IF the operator does not add an independent verification step before acting on validation results
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for generated validation inputs
Compare outputs against source-of-truth data
Log provenance for each artifact consumed by Great Expectations
Fail closed when artifact schema changes
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no PHI, residency, or certification mismatch. Argo touches artifacts and parameters; Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation. With no documented regulated data class or jurisdictional constraint, compliance risk is limited to documentation/retention handling if the operator routes sensitive data through them.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into artifacts, validation results, or documentation
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Apply a common retention policy to shared outputs
Document where validation results are stored
Review exports for sensitive fields before sharing
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement to the pipeline
